Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.fertilizer: Maintain balanced fertility without excessive nitrogen
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.pesticide: Apply copper bactericide combined with mancozeb for maximum effect
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds and avoid overhead irrigation

Pepper__bell___healthy.fertilizer: Use calcium and magnesium rich fertilizers to prevent blossom end rot
Pepper__bell___healthy.prevention: Mulch soil and ensure even watering

Potato___Early_blight.fertilizer: Ensure adequate nitrogen and phosphorus throughout the season
Potato___Early_blight.pesticide: Use azoxystrobin or chlorothalonil during early detection
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Use certified seed, allow tubers to mature fully before harvest

Potato___Late_blight.fertilizer: Avoid over-fertilizing with nitrogen to prevent lush, vulnerable canopies
Potato___Late_blight.pesticide: Apply preventative fungicides immediately when cool, wet weather persists
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Remove volunteer potatoes, plant resistant varieties

Potato___healthy.fertilizer: Apply standard recommended NPK for potatoes
Potato___healthy.prevention: Keep weeds under control and maintain even soil moisture

Tomato_Bacterial_spot.fertilizer: Avoid excessive nitrogen, which can promote susceptible foliage growth.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.pesticide: Apply copper-based bactericides early in the infection cycle.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.prevention: Ensure good air circulation and avoid overhead irrigation.

Tomato_Early_blight.fertilizer: Apply potassium-rich fertilizer to strengthen the plant
Tomato_Early_blight.prevention: Remove infected leaves, avoid watering from above, rotate crops each season

Tomato_Late_blight.fertilizer: Avoid excess nitrogen. Use balanced NPK soil additives
Tomato_Late_blight.pesticide: Apply chlorothalonil or mancozeb as soon as conditions are wet and cool
Tomato_Late_blight.prevention: Destroy culled potatoes, keep foliage dry, space plants well

Tomato_Leaf_Mold.fertilizer: Maintain balanced fertility to ensure robust growth
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.prevention: Ensure good ventilation, reduce humidity, prune lower leaves

Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.fertilizer: Regular balanced feeding to support vigorous new growth.
Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.pesticide: Use preventative fungicidal sprays such as chlorothalonil.
Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Mulch to prevent soil splash and practice crop rotation.

Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.fertilizer: Maintain plant vigor; drought-stressed plants are highly susceptible.
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.pesticide: Use insecticidal soaps, neem oil, or selective miticides.
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.prevention: Keep plants well-watered and wash foliage periodically to deter mites.

Tomato__Target_Spot.fertilizer: Ensure sufficient air flow to reduce canopy humidity rather than modifying fertilizer.
Tomato__Target_Spot.pesticide: Mancozeb or copper-based treatments when symptoms first appear.
Tomato__Target_Spot.prevention: Increase plant spacing and avoid excessive overhead watering.

Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.fertilizer: Maintain optimal nutrition to help plants tolerate the virus.
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.pesticide: Apply insecticides to control whiteflies (the virus vector).
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.prevention: Use virus-resistant tomato varieties and control whitefly populations.

Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.fertilizer: Standard feeding; virus cannot be cured with fertilizer.
Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Disinfect tools, avoid tobacco use near plants, and plant resistant varieties.

Tomato_healthy.fertilizer: Continue current regular feeding with balanced nutrients
Tomato_healthy.prevention: Maintain consistent watering and watch for pests
